denormal-fp-math.reason: already taught as a departure: named in the rename table at 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:82, which states that it folded into `denormal_fpenv` — the one thing a reader of older IR or older build files needs. No chapter ever taught the string attribute itself (grep: it occurs only at reference/llvm-surface-18.json:90), because it was a build-configuration string inside the `attributes #N` group line that the corpus's normalizer drops (tools/verify-frontend-lowering.py:52). denormal-fp-math-f32.reason: already taught as a departure: 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:83 names it and its fold into `denormal_fpenv`. It was the f32-specific override of the same build-configuration string — its whole content was "and float is different", which the new attribute expresses as a second component — and it appears in the corpus only at reference/llvm-surface-18.json:91, never in a chapter, never in an example, and never in a snapshot line the normalizer keeps.

denormal_fpenv.reason: Build-configuration knob, not lowering, and it never reaches a line the corpus shows. Checked: clang-23 emits `denormal_fpenv(preservesign)` only when the build passes -fdenormal-fp-math=; plain -O1, -ffast-math and -ffp-model=fast all emit nothing, and when it does appear it is inside the `attributes #0 = {...}` group line, which the snapshot normalizer drops entirely (tools/verify-frontend-lowering.py:52 _DROP_LINE). No chapter teaches either spelling (grep: `denormal-fp-math` occurs only in reference/llvm-surface-18.json:90-91), and the rename is already named at 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:82-83. Teaching it would require opening FP-environment and denormal modes, which the corpus does not cover anywhere.

flatten.reason: clang cannot put it in your IR. Checked: clang-23 accepts `__attribute__((flatten))` without complaint but emits no `flatten` attribute at -O0 or -O1, with an inlinable callee and with a `noinline` callee — the attribute group is `{ noinline nounwind optnone ... }` / `{ nounwind uwtable ... }` in every case. The IR attribute (Attributes.td:137-138, "Flatten function by recursively inlining all calls") is a directive for non-clang frontends and pass authors, lives in the dropped attributes-group line, and the corpus teaches inlining by its observable effect in 07-optimization rather than by directive. The 14 corpus files matching "flatten" all use the English word ("lowering flattens this structure"), never the attribute.

hybrid_patchable.reason: Arm64EC-only: it marks a function that also needs an x64-emulation-compatible thunk under the Windows-on-Arm hybrid ABI, written by `__declspec(hybrid_patchable)`. Every target triple in the corpus's 209 .ll files is x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (92), unknown-unknown-unknown (13), x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (2), riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu (2) or x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (1) — no arm64ec — so it cannot appear in any IR the corpus builds or a reader following it produces. The corpus already names Windows/MSVC ABI specifics as a boundary rather than a subject (16-exception-handling covers the SEH/funclet side it does teach).

llvm.experimental.stepvector.reason: already taught: 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:100 lists this exact rename in the graduation table, with the stability-marker meaning of `llvm.experimental.` at :107 and the pinned-to-a-release consequence at :112. Its graduated form llvm.stepvector is marked taught in this group for its semantics, so the pair is covered from both sides — the naming event where the corpus already teaches naming events, the operation where the corpus teaches scalable vectors. Nothing is left for a separate section.

llvm.experimental.vector.compress.reason: lane compaction — pack the active lanes toward the low end, preserving order — backing AVX-512 vcompress and SVE compact. It arrived in LLVM 23 still carrying the `experimental.` prefix, so it is on the in-flight side of the very pipeline 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:107 describes, and pinning its spelling in a chapter is what SEMVER.md:11 ('Prefer IR syntax that remains stable across supported LLVM versions') tells this corpus not to do. Its longer-standing memory-side cousins llvm.masked.compressstore and llvm.masked.expandload predate LLVM 18 and the corpus already declines to teach those.

llvm.experimental.vector.deinterleave2.reason: already taught: 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:104 lists `llvm.experimental.vector.deinterleave2 -> llvm.vector.deinterleave2` in the graduation table. The operation is also already taught end to end: 09-vectorization/07-masked-and-interleaved-access.md:11 introduces AoS-to-SoA deinterleaving, :24 points at examples/interleaved-access-after-vectorize.ll, and :127-128 shows the portable fixed-width form as two constant-mask shufflevectors.

llvm.experimental.vector.extract.last.ac.reason: extracts the lane at the highest set position of a mask; the loop vectorizer emits it for 'last match wins' search loops. Still `experimental.`-spelled in LLVM 23, so it sits in the staging namespace 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:107 warns readers not to hard-code. The reader's underlying need — get one lane out of a vector — is `extractelement`, already taught at reference/instruction-quickref.md:249 and 02-types/02-composite-types.md:13; this intrinsic only supplies a mask-derived index.

llvm.experimental.vector.histogram.add.reason: masked scatter-with-conflict-detection that increments memory locations which may repeat within a single vector — emitted only when the loop vectorizer recognizes a histogram idiom AND the target has conflict detection (AVX-512CD vpconflict, SVE2 histcnt). The generalizable question is whether lanes of one vector iteration can collide, which 09-vectorization/04-vectorization-legality.md:32 ('No unsafe dependencies') and :69 ('Loop-carried dependencies') already teach; this is one target-gated answer, still experimental-spelled.

llvm.experimental.vector.histogram.uadd..reason: saturating-add variant of the LLVM 23 histogram family, for histogram loops whose bucket counters must clamp instead of wrap. It combines two things the corpus declines separately — the target-gated conflict-detection idiom (09-vectorization/04-vectorization-legality.md:32 teaches the underlying dependence question) and saturating arithmetic, whose generic form llvm.uadd.sat the corpus does not teach either — and it is still `experimental.`-spelled in LLVM 23.

llvm.experimental.vector.histogram.umax.reason: unsigned-max variant of the LLVM 23 histogram family, for 'record the largest value seen per bucket' loops. Same target gating as the rest of the family (AVX-512CD, SVE2 histcnt) and same still-experimental spelling; the transferable content is the intra-vector collision question already taught at 09-vectorization/04-vectorization-legality.md:32 and :69.

llvm.experimental.vector.histogram.umin.reason: unsigned-min variant of the LLVM 23 histogram family, the mirror of histogram.umax. It is vectorizer idiom-recognition output for one loop shape on targets with conflict detection, not a construct a reader writes, and it still carries the `experimental.` prefix that 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:149 tells readers not to hard-code.

llvm.experimental.vector.interleave2.reason: already taught: 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:103 lists `llvm.experimental.vector.interleave2 -> llvm.vector.interleave2` in the graduation table. It is a pure rename, and the corpus already teaches the operation at fixed width — reference/instruction-quickref.md:108 names 'interleaves lanes' as a shufflevector role and 09-vectorization/07-masked-and-interleaved-access.md teaches interleaved-group recognition throughout.

llvm.experimental.vector.match.reason: tests whether each lane's value appears anywhere in a second, small search vector — the SVE2 MATCH primitive behind vectorized strchr/strcspn-style searches, which lowers to one instruction on SVE2 and to an O(N*M) comparison chain elsewhere. That target-shaped profitability cliff is exactly the boundary 13-advanced-ir/02-target-specific-intrinsics.md draws, and the name is still `experimental.`-spelled in LLVM 23.

llvm.experimental.vector.reverse.reason: already taught: 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:101 lists `llvm.experimental.vector.reverse -> llvm.vector.reverse` in the graduation table, and it is a pure rename — no signature or semantic change to record. The operation is separately reachable from what the corpus already teaches: reference/instruction-quickref.md:108 lists 'reverses ... lanes' as a shufflevector role, so a reader knows the fixed-width form and needs only the scalable-vector reason the intrinsic exists.

llvm.experimental.vector.splice.reason: already taught, but with a defect this group fixes rather than duplicates: 23-village is not the citation — 23-version-movement/01-reading-the-delta.md:102 lists this departure in the graduation table, and its stated replacement `llvm.vector.splice` does not exist in LLVM 23 (reference/llvm-surface-23.json has only llvm.vector.splice.left and llvm.vector.splice.right). The departure itself is correctly recorded and correctly explained by the surrounding graduation rule at :107 and :112; the wrong half is the arrival name, which is why llvm.vector.splice.left and llvm.vector.splice.right are the taught items. Fixing that row covers this departure too.

llvm.masked.sdiv.reason: new in LLVM 23 and the first llvm.masked.* members that are not memory operations, but the rule underneath is one the corpus already owns. Signed division cannot be speculated — sdiv by zero and sdiv INT_MIN/-1 are immediate undefined behavior — so a predicated sdiv cannot be lowered as compute-all-lanes-then-select the way a predicated add can. That is the safe-speculation rule taught at 13-advanced-ir/05-poison-undef-freeze.md:144 ('BCIR safe speculation with `freeze`') applied to one opcode, plus the mask-as-legality-device rule taught at 09-vectorization/07-masked-and-interleaved-access.md:144. The corpus's masked-family coverage deliberately stops at load/store (reference/intrinsics-quickref.md:81-82), where the mask governs memory legality.

llvm.masked.srem.reason: predicated signed remainder, new in LLVM 23 for the same reason as llvm.masked.sdiv: srem by zero and srem INT_MIN/-1 are immediate undefined behavior, so inactive lanes must genuinely not execute rather than be selected away afterward. The generalizable content is the speculation rule at 13-advanced-ir/05-poison-undef-freeze.md:144, not the intrinsic spelling, and 15-binary-analysis/01-microarchitecture-side-channels.md:29 already flags srem as a variable-latency operation a reader should notice.

llvm.masked.udiv.reason: predicated unsigned division, new in LLVM 23. Division by zero is immediate undefined behavior, which is why a masked form is needed at all instead of an unmasked udiv plus select — the corpus already teaches both halves of that reasoning: the safe-speculation rule at 13-advanced-ir/05-poison-undef-freeze.md:144, and 09-vectorization/03-vector-predication.md's Pitfalls, which states that `select` prevents a value from being chosen but requires both operands to already be safe to compute.

llvm.masked.urem.reason: predicated unsigned remainder, new in LLVM 23, sharing the div-by-zero undefined-behavior reason that makes select-after-the-fact illegal for this opcode family. The rule is taught at 13-advanced-ir/05-poison-undef-freeze.md:144 and 09-vectorization/03-vector-predication.md Pitfalls; the corpus keeps its llvm.masked.* coverage at load/store, where the mask is a memory-legality device (09-vectorization/07-masked-and-interleaved-access.md:98).

nodivergencesource.reason: GPU uniformity analysis: it promises a call introduces no new divergence, and it is consumed by the divergence/uniformity analysis that only AMDGPU and NVPTX run. The corpus teaches the other half of this story deliberately and stops there — `convergent` and the wavefront/subgroup model at 13-advanced-ir/03-special-types-and-tokens.md:53-58, and the `convergencectrl` bundle at reference/intrinsics-quickref.md:279-287 — and no corpus example uses a GPU triple. Checked: no CPU-target clang-23 invocation in my probes emitted it.

noext.reason: The third member of a family whose other two the corpus already teaches: `signext` / `zeroext` at 01-syntax/01-modules-functions-blocks.md:120 and 05-control-flow/05-call-and-ret.md:213. `noext` says the ABI leaves a narrow argument's high bits unspecified, which is a live question only on ABIs like SystemZ's that would otherwise mandate extension. Checked: clang-23 emits `signext`/`zeroext` and never `noext` for i1/i8/i16 parameters and returns on both x86_64-linux and s390x-linux — including in a declaration-only call across a translation unit — so a reader on the corpus's triples will not meet it.

noipa.reason: Not reachable from clang at all. Checked: clang-23 rejects it — "warning: unknown attribute 'noipa' ignored [-Wunknown-attributes]" — so it cannot appear in clang output; it is a GCC-compatibility attribute that GCC-compatible frontends emit, meaning "do no interprocedural analysis across this function". Its effect is the pessimistic corner of the interprocedural behaviour 07-optimization already teaches through pass behaviour, and it rides in the dropped `attributes #N` group line rather than on any instruction.

nooutline.reason: Double opt-in and a pass level the corpus does not cover. Checked: clang-23 rejects the IR spelling as a source attribute ("unknown attribute 'nooutline' ignored; did you mean 'no_outline'?") and emits `nooutline` into the `attributes #0` group only when the source writes `__attribute__((no_outline))` — so it appears exclusively because the reader put it there. It opts a function out of the MachineOutliner, a MIR-level pass; grep finds no chapter mentioning the outliner (the "outlin" hits in exercises are about outlining a lowering, not the pass), and 12-backend-jit stops above MIR passes.

range.note: Zero occurrences of `range(` anywhere in the corpus (grep over all .md and .ll), while clang-23 -O2 puts it on ordinary returns: `define dso_local range(i32 0, 2) i32 @cmpc(...)` for `return c < 128;` and `range(i32 0, 8)` for `return i & 7;`. sanitize_alloc_token.reason: Verified emitted only under `-fsanitize=alloc-token`, and only in the `attributes #N` group line the normalizer drops (tools/verify-frontend-lowering.py:52). It marks a function for the allocation-token pass that rewrites allocator calls; the corpus's sanitizer teaching is deliberately about instrumentation you must not delete — shadow-address arithmetic, check branches, `!nosanitize` (08-pitfalls/16-sanitizer-instrumentation.md) — and teaches no sanitize_* attribute at all, not even the LLVM 18-era `sanitize_address`, so this opens no new gap relative to what the corpus covers.

sanitize_numerical_stability.reason: Verified emitted only under `-fsanitize=numerical` (NSan, which shadows every FP computation in higher precision to catch instability), and only in the dropped `attributes #N` group line. Nothing in the corpus's FP material (the fast-math risk review at exercises/027, 08-pitfalls FP chapters) depends on the marker: the reader who turned NSan on chose it, and what they then read in the IR is the shadow-FP instrumentation, which is the same shape 08-pitfalls/16-sanitizer-instrumentation.md already teaches for the address case.

sanitize_realtime.reason: Doubly opt-in. Checked: `-fsanitize=realtime` alone put nothing on an ordinary function — RTSan attaches this only to functions the source marks `[[clang::nonblocking]]`, so both the flag and the source annotation must be the reader's own choice. It marks the real-time constraint region for a runtime that traps on blocking calls; the corpus teaches no real-time or nonblocking-function contract anywhere, and the attribute lives in the dropped `attributes #N` group line.

sanitize_realtime_blocking.reason: The complement of sanitize_realtime, attached to functions the source marks `[[clang::blocking]]` under `-fsanitize=realtime`; same double opt-in, verified the same way (nothing appears on an unannotated function). It is bookkeeping for the RTSan runtime rather than a fact about the IR's meaning: no instruction's semantics change, and it never leaves the `attributes #N` group line the corpus's snapshots drop.

sanitize_type.reason: Verified emitted only under `-fsanitize=type` (TySan, which checks type-based aliasing violations at runtime), in the dropped `attributes #N` group line. The corpus already teaches the static half of this subject where a reader actually needs it — TBAA metadata at 06-metadata (tbaa-load-store.ll) and the aliasing pitfalls at 08-pitfalls/12 — and teaches no sanitize_* attribute; the marker adds nothing to reading either.
